takes.h: The pulps were meant to fall apart
takes.p: Pulp paper was chosen because it was cheap, and cheap paper browns and crumbles. Every surviving copy of a twenties or thirties horror pulp is an accident of storage. Handle them like the near-miracles they are, and buy the reprints for the actual reading.

The remaster that fixes a muddy mix is welcome. The remaster that brick-walls a record so it competes with modern loudness is not. If the original pressing breathes and the new one shouts, keep the original on the turntable and file the reissue under bonus material.

A reprint line makes two promises at once: to the collector, that the original stays rare, and to the reader, that the book is finally available. Both are worth keeping. The good presses manage it by printing well, introducing the book honestly, and getting out of its way.
